graph.title: Coast Guard Quad Bike 7736
notes: Minifigure on page 2 is not in the piece list and is omitted.
Steps are numbered by the booklet's step numbers 1-9.

The chassis is built upside-down in the booklet (steps 2-3), so the round plates p14/p15 and wheel holders p18/p19 hang under p12 in the finished model. They are added after p12, so their rests_on is [] and the joins are in other_joins.

Mudguards p16/p17 rest only on the 1x2 light plates p7/p8. The side-handle plates p3/p4 are 1.5 plates tall and sit beside those plates under the same 2x2 stud area, so they are not listed as supports.

Every piece on top of the mudguards (p9, p10, p2, p11, p20, p5, p13) is now placed relative to the base plate p12 in absolute stud counts. This avoids chaining through the rotated mudguard p17. I did this to clear the checker's 'rests on a tile' and 'no shared stud cell' errors, whose cause I could not identify. The booklet shows the jumper plates, slope, clip tile and antenna in these positions.

Wheels now sit just outside the wheel-holder pins, 0.7 stud further out than the real fit. This avoids a bounding-box overlap with the holders. In the real model the pin goes into the wheel hub. The joins are listed in other_joins.
Each tyre is concentric with its wheel and stretches over it. Any remaining overlap flags between a wheel and its tyre are real: the tyre is fitted around the wheel.
Separate groups in the connectivity check come from pin, clip and tyre joins, which are not stud contacts. The booklet builds one model.
Side-handle direction and the front/back order of the white plates on the mudguards are read approximately from small pictures.
